title: Math formulas, level 1: shapes and solids
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Perimeter, area and volume come up everywhere: painting a wall, fencing a garden, filling a fish tank. Each formula is short, and each one makes sense once you see where it comes from.

How to hold it: Don't memorize these as strings of letters; rebuild them from a picture. Area of a rectangle is rows times columns of unit squares (l x w). A triangle is half a rectangle, so one-half b h. A parallelogram is a rectangle with one end slid over, so b h. Volume stacks area in layers. Draw each shape with its formula beside it (picture plus words), then recall it on a blank page and check.
This list has 12 items. Answer below, then check — the practice button generates fresh questions from the list itself.
